title: feat: safe program starts, owner push yes and fewer false holds
headline: Every program the installed kit starts by name now starts from node's own folder; an owner push past the bound needs the owner's yes; reviewers read rules from the merge base; and harmless reads the guards held now pass.
alignment: v1.49.0 is build 23a of the v2.0 plan: K250 first, then K209, K212 to K215, K211, R7.1 with K224, K217, K243, K244, K218, K210, K207, K208, K204, K251, K226 to K229, K241, K242, K252, K154 and K186, each reproduced on the released 1.48.0 or proven by a failing test first.

items.text: On Windows the guard start script left the launcher no git, so a project with git's worktree config on had every tool call held; the launcher now gets Git for Windows' own folder, never the session's PATH.
items.test: tests/guards-outside.test.mjs::the guard start script lets the launcher find git, never a git planted on the session PATH (K250)

items.text: On a Mac or Linux machine whose git sits in /usr/local/bin or /opt/homebrew/bin, the guard start script finds it, after the system folders.
items.test: tests/guards-outside.test.mjs::the guard start script gives the launcher the system folders, then the Mac and Linux git folders

items.text: One safe-spawn helper starts every installed kit launch (git, gh, ps) from node's own folder, with a time limit, so a git.exe or gh.exe left in a project never runs.

verification: Worktree config on Windows: the kit's own test fails at 1.48.0 on the owner's PC and passes here; a new test fails on the 1.48.0 start script and on a session-PATH version, and passes here.

A throwaway install of this branch (worktree config on, 70 folders): plain reads, the K154 and K252 shapes and git status run through the installed chain; a guard write, a globbing write and a push to main are held.
The spawn check reports 0 unsafe bare-name launches, down from 45; both guard self-checks pass (779 and 301 cases).

decisions.decision: The launcher gets Git for Windows' own folder, not the session's PATH
decisions.why: A session PATH could hold a planted git.

decisions.decision: A wildcard in inline node code is text only where the code can reach no file
decisions.why: The owner's pick (2026-11-21); code that lists, writes or runs is read strictly.

decisions.decision: An owner push marker needs a pop-up yes per ref

decisions.why: New holds and checks reach every project.

decisions.decision: The K229 test reads `find -delete` from the `.claude` folder
decisions.why: Its first case held only by its pipe.

decisions.decision: A short closeout answer needs its own row
decisions.why: decide records no words_from below three words.

decisions.decision: Four sweep findings closed with no change
decisions.why: The sweep report gives each reason.
125 probes gave the same decision before and after.

decisions.decision: The owner push rule line is reworded in build 23b
decisions.why: The owner's pick (2026-11-21): a rewording needs a paid recall run, and the hook's refusal already names the typed ref.

upgrading: Run install user, then install project: the guard start script, the launcher, the commit-msg and pre-push hooks, owner-proof, owner-yes, the safe-spawn helper copies, name-check, state.mjs, loop.mjs and the closeout and brainstorm skills change. The owner's own push now asks for the ref's name at their terminal (or a pop-up yes in a session); a person whose name matches a code tool commits once listed with `git config --add kit.allowedIdent "<name> <email>"`.
limits: Inline code can still build a path from pieces no guard reads; the narrow K154 reading trusts only code with no file, list or run call. A rules file the base does not hold is read from the main checkout, as before. The owner's typed ref is read from their terminal: a tool that can type into that terminal could answer it. The author check knows eight code tools and five maker domains; another name passes, and the hook is skipped where name-check.mjs is missing or the owner commits with `--no-verify`. The kit's git reads take attributes from the empty tree (git 2.40 or later; an older git ignores it), so line-ending attributes fall to core.autocrlf there; a clean filter named in the repo's own info/attributes still runs on a status, its program set only in git config, which no tool writes. The closeout reads only this session's transcript: a card answered in a project thread is not seen, and two answers with the same words need a row each. A flag or subcommand built at run time beyond a plain expansion is not read.
